note: Evergreen guidance maintained by the VigilPay team. Add dated advisories here as official sources publish them.

items.title: 'Digital arrest' and fake police or courier calls
items.text: Callers pose as police, CBI or customs, claim a parcel has drugs or you are linked to a crime, and keep you on a video call while demanding money.
tips: Hang up. There is no 'digital arrest' in Indian law.
Real agencies never ask you to pay to close a case.
Tell a family member and call 1930 if you are unsure.

items.title: Part-time job and 'task' scams
items.text: You are paid a small amount for liking videos or rating products, then asked to deposit larger amounts to unlock bigger payouts that never arrive.
tips: Never pay to earn.
Be wary of jobs that come only through Telegram or WhatsApp groups.
Save chats and transaction IDs, then report.

items.title: Guaranteed-return trading and investment groups
items.text: Fake experts promise guaranteed profits through apps and groups. Early 'profits' on screen cannot be withdrawn.
tips: No legitimate investment guarantees high returns.
Check that an adviser or platform is registered with the regulator before paying.
Do not install apps shared in chat groups.

items.title: 'Scan to receive' QR codes and collect requests
items.text: Sellers and buyers on marketplaces are told to scan a QR or approve a request to 'receive' money. Both actions send money out.
tips: You never need a PIN to receive money.
Give only your UPI ID to a buyer.
Decline unknown collect requests.

items.title: Fake KYC, blocked-account and electricity-bill messages
items.text: Messages threaten that your account, SIM or power will be cut tonight unless you call a number, click a link or install an app.
tips: Do not call numbers in the message.
Use the official app or the number on your card.
Report suspect numbers on the Sanchar Saathi portal.

items.title: Malicious .apk files sent as challans, KYC or scheme updates
items.text: A file sent on chat is presented as an RTO challan, bank update or government scheme. Installing it can give attackers your SMS and OTPs.
tips: Never install apps from chat or SMS.
If you did, switch to airplane mode and uninstall it.
Then call your bank and 1930.

items.title: 'I am your relative in trouble' messages
items.text: Scammers copy a photo and name, claim a lost phone or an emergency, and ask for quick payment to a new account.
tips: Call the real person on their old number.
Agree a family code word.
Do not pay until you have confirmed.

items.title: Fake refund, cashback and customer-care numbers
items.text: A number found in a search result or social post gets you to install remote apps or share OTPs to 'process a refund'.
tips: Use only the helpline inside the official app or on the official site.
Refunds are credited automatically.
Never share an OTP to get money.
